quest.title: The Narukami Trail
quest.description: Neko, "Provisional Head Priestess of the Asase Shrine," seems to have something she wants to do...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x5

talks.objective: Go near the Grand Narukami Shrine

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: "Grand Narukami Shrine"... Is this the place?

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: There are so many red doors. Do humans like red doors a lot?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is called a "torii gate."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They are at Asase Shrine too.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Oh, I understand now. So, this is a "torii gate." It's a place where birds live, right?

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: So the more torii gates there are, the more birds there are, right? Birds are a good thing. Humans are pretty smart, too.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Have you seen where Hibiki is?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no trace of anyone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There seems to be no one around...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why don't we go up to the Grand Narukami Shrine and ask the shrine maidens there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Hibiki" should also be a shrine maiden... Maybe they would know something.

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Narukami Shrine

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Meow, this shrine is really big, and there are a lot of humans too.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Wow! The Offering Box and racks are also very grand, no wonder so many people come here.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: You should take some pointers. In the future, Asase Shrine will become like this.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: However, I still don't see Hibiki anywhere.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's find someone to ask about "Hibiki."

choices.text: Wait, why am I the one who has to take some pointers?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler from afar. Welcome to the Grand Narukami Shrine!

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: If you encounter any trouble or just want to make a wish, feel free to come here for a fortune slip. May the Electro Archon bless you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We are not here to ask for a fortune slip, but there is something we want to ask you...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Ask me? Oh... go ahead then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, here's the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Hibiki from Asase Shrine? Could it be "Asase Hibiki"...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Yes! Hibiki is "Asase Hibiki." Human! Do you know Hibiki? Do you know where she is?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Hmmm... Huh!? How can this cat talk? Am I hearing things...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Humans, such ado about nothing... Is it so strange that I speak?

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Do you know Hibiki? Do you know where she is?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: It feels really strange to be questioned by a cat...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: However, if you are really asking about that "Asase Hibiki," you've come to the wrong place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wrong... place?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: I have come across her name in the few well-preserved ancient texts of the shrine. She is the last successor of Asase Shrine...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: About four to five hundred years ago, it was said that "The Yougou Three" Asase Hibiki, Kamuna Harunosuke, and Mikoshi Nagamasa once went to Mt. Yougou to learn under the Yougou Tengu.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: During that time, Asase apprenticed at our shrine and also befriended the Kitsune Saiguu. However, in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: The three eventually parted ways after a "disaster" that was vague in their account. It is said that Kamuna Harunosuke crossed the sea and went to Liyue as he wanted to learn the more powerful "way of the adepti."

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Mikoshi Nagamasa returned to Inazuma City to serve the Shogunate. As for Asase Hibiki...

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Well, that's right. But because there is so little historical information available, the details are not very clear.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait a minute...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... she said four to five hundred years ago. So that means, Hibiki was someone from a long time ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Neko's a cat that's 400 or 500 years old?

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Meow? I'm not sure. What does "400 or 500 years old" mean?

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: I am not a human being. There aren't many things to worry about. I just know the rising of the sun, and then the moon. If I am in a bad mood, sleep is the best remedy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's so envious...

choices.text: Paimon, it's almost the same for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! How rude, Paimon is worried sick about {NICKNAME} every day.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: You have said a lot of things that I do not understand. So, where is Hibiki?

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: With all due respect, I'm afraid that Asase Hibiki has...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hibiki is not here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, that's right. Hibiki should have gone somewhere else.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: That's true.

response.speaker: Neko
response.text: Oh well. Hibiki is still like a child, running around as she pleases.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, thank you, Miss Shrine Maiden!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Please excuse us, we'll be leaving now.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Take care now. I'll be ready to help whenever you need me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Generally speaking, not really...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Let's have a rest here, I am tired.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: But it's really the same as what Hibiki said.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: The different islands are really completely different. Also, it turns out that the shrine can be on such a high mountain. Aren't humans afraid of heights?

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: My Asase Shrine is still better.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Where exactly is Hibiki, I wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you still wish to continue looking for her?

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: I am tired. Let's talk about it later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's still a "later"!?

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: That's for sure. Hibiki told me many, many stories. Stories about the beach, stories about the place with lots of trees, stories about the "Lady Kitsune."

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: I remember all these stories very well.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: But the most important thing now is to return home. After all, Asase Shrine must have its Guuji.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: In short, you will go back with me now.

talks.objective: Return with Neko to Seirai Island

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Phew... finally back. After staying next to that shrine for a long time, my fur is curling up.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for your help. You are truly a rare and reliable human being, meow.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: I will continue to take care of the shrine. When Hibiki returns, I will introduce you to her.

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Meow, meow...

dialogues.speaker: Neko
dialogues.text: Ah, when will Hibiki come back...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Is something the matter?

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Legend has it that Mikoshi Nagamasa has been working for the Shogunate, and it is said that he is extremely just and upright, even to the point of... being overly stubborn.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: His bloodline has been passed down to this day. Most of the people in the city who have the surname Mikoshi today are his descendants.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: There aren't many records about him. He returned to Inazuma after crossing the sea to Liyue to learn the art of the adepti.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Then, he created his own "Onmyoudou" and "Shiki Taishou."

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: According to the records, in order to bring peace to Inazuma, he once used this technique to seal the bake-danuki, Ioroi, that was making trouble everywhere.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: But later, news of him gradually disappeared.

response.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
response.text: Take care now. I'll be ready to help whenever you need me.
